2400: They called boarding by group number, and somehow every single person decided their group was being called now.
2401: A bag nudged through the rubber flaps, paused dramatically, and slid out to belong to somebody who was not you.
2402: The belt jolted to life, everyone leaned in at once, and it proudly delivered a single taped-up cardboard box.
2403: Three bags in a row looked exactly like yours. You checked all three tags. All three belonged to strangers.
2404: You reached for a bag, read the tag, apologized to it quietly, and set it gently back on its way.
2405: You opened the overhead bin with great confidence, and a stranger's heavy coat slid gently down onto your head.
2406: The seatbelt light clicked off and half the plane stood up at once, to wait, standing, in a line that went nowhere.
2407: A child pointed at the moving belt and asked, very reasonably, whether people were allowed to ride it. They are not.
2408: One happy traveler grabbed their bag on the very first turn and strolled off, insufferably and unforgivably lucky.
2409: The screen picked a belt, then changed its mind, and the whole crowd shuffled off to a completely different one.
2410: A suitcase wrapped in so much plastic it looked ready for the ocean floor rolled past, sealed and enormously proud.
2411: You handed over your passport, and the photo inside looked like a distant cousin who still owes you money.
2412: The flaps at the top of the chute burst open and out tumbled three bags at once in a small luggage avalanche.
2413: You saw your bag, reached out, and it slid smoothly past your fingers to begin one more entire unnecessary lap.
2414: They asked if you had anything to declare. Only a deep exhaustion, and you doubted it was the taxable kind.
2415: The belt curved at the corner and the bags bunched up at the bend, a small and very polite traffic jam.
2416: A single shoe rode by on the belt, alone and completely dignified, and not one person moved to claim it.
2417: You leaned across two strangers, seized the handle, and hauled your bag up with a grunt you would later deny.
2418: Two hands reached for the same suitcase, froze, and each waved the other on with pained, generous politeness.
2419: You loaded bags onto a cart one at a time and felt, briefly, like a very small but extremely organized crane.
2420: You stepped onto the moving walkway and, for ten glorious seconds, felt like the fastest person ever born.
2421: You lifted your bag off the belt in one smooth motion and glanced around to see who noticed. Nobody did.
2422: A suitcase arrived with a loose strap flapping behind it, waving at the whole crowd like it had stories to tell.
2423: You realized, three full laps in, that you had been faithfully and confidently guarding the wrong belt the whole time.
2424: When your bag finally rolled into view, you greeted it with more open relief than you have shown most relatives.
2425: You reached the bottom of a long staircase, looked up at every step of it, and began quietly negotiating with your legs.
2426: Everyone stared at their phones between glances at the belt, heads snapping up in unison each time it clicked.
2427: You bought a coffee to feel human again, and the price alone woke you up faster than the coffee ever could.

2429: A golf bag the size of a small canoe rounded the corner, and everyone in the crowd quietly hoped it was not theirs.

2431: You leaned against a pillar with your arms folded, radiating the calm of a person who was absolutely not worried yet.
